page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the n2 server family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the n2-highmem-4 primarily in the lower performance tiers. Both single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench rank in the bottom 25%. Similarly, memory bandwidth for large block reads and writes falls into the bottom 25%, though PassMark memory scores and single-threaded gzip compression achieve average tier results. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware-level instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES, though database operations and Redis SET throughput remain in the bottom 25% tier.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its low compute-to-memory ratio, where memory capacity is prioritized over raw processing speed. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-4 provides a dense memory allocation per vCPU, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense parallel CPU processing. Appropriate workloads include small-scale database hosting, caching layers, memory-intensive text processing, and general-purpose applications requiring a larger memory footprint than standard compute instances.
